title: Console friction mapping — mid-sprint standup notes
content:
Context: quick, focused mid-sprint sync to map out UX friction points around the recent rollout gate change, surface analytics mismatches, and lock down a canary rehearsal checklist. Mostly informal notes + action list.

Attendees: Samira (owner), Marco, Leah, Ethan, Jessie (observability), QA: Aisha joined for the last 10m.

Agenda:
- 5m: current rollout gate state and incidence summary
- 10m: friction map (where users/operators hit confusion)
- 10m: analytics discrepancies and telemetry gaps
- 10m: action items + rehearsal checklist for tomorrow's canary

Summary / quick TL;DR:
- Gate change (config-driven gate v2) landed on 2027-05-12. No user-facing outages but several operator confusion points + two dashboards showing divergent counts for "panel-apply" events vs API-side logs.
- Root cause appears to be (a) event sampling config mismatch between frontend telemetry and backend ingestion, and (b) ambiguous panel states in the UI when rollout is partially applied.
- We agreed to roll forward with a short patch for telemetry (drop-in sampling alignment) and a UX microcopy update to make panel states explicit. Canary rehearsal planned 2027-05-19 09:30 PT.

Friction map (observed + reported):
- Ambiguous state: panel shows "Applying" for 60s then jumps to "Active" with no intermediate logs. Operators expected a progress bar, not a spinner. (Reported in slack thread #console-ops)
- Rollout metadata missing: rollout id and commit hash are not shown in the UI route panel, making it hard to reconcile with infra logs.
- Telemetry sampling: frontend configured to sample 1/100 events for analytics, but ingestion pipeline assumes 1/10; derived metrics are therefore off by ~10x for a subset of events.
- Alert noise: a duplicate alert fires when partial apply + backend timeout occurs; duplicate is from two alert rules that both look at different metrics but same symptom.
- Observability blindspot: KV cache warmup events for canaried variants are not instrumented; we lose visibility into latency spikes during early traffic shift.

Evidence and quick repro notes:
- Repro: Local repro steps in GH PR checklist (see linked PR). Toggle feature-flag X in staging, apply rollout with 10% traffic, observe UI spinner -> active transition at ~60s while server logs show apply completed at ~8s.
- Dashboards: panel-apply-events (frontend) vs panel-apply-log-lines (backend) mismatch; query snapshots attached in PR comments.

Decisions made in this sync:
- Telemetry fix first: standardize sampling to ingestion by shipping a telemetry config override in UI (feature flag telemetry-sampling-fixed). Target deploy: 2027-05-18 EOD to staging. Owner: Marco.
- UX microcopy: change "Applying" -> "Applying (waiting for backend confirm)" and add small help tooltip linking to rollout docs. Target PR: console#1876. Owner: Leah.
- Alerts: dedupe two related alert rules and add a short-circuit condition: only fire if "backend-apply-errors" > 0 and UI-apply-duration > 20s. Owner: Jessie (observability).
- Instrument KV cache warmup events: add telemetry event "kv-warmup" on first request after variant switch. Owner: Ethan (platform). Ship to staging with low sampling.

Action items (owner — due):
- Marco — push telemetry sampling override to staging (2027-05-18) — include QA smoke script.
- Leah — open UI microcopy PR and add screenshots for design review (2027-05-18) — link in doc when ready.
- Jessie — update alert rules, add dedupe logic, and create runbook note for this symptom (2027-05-19).
- Ethan — instrument kv-warmup event and add example query to analytics dashboard (2027-05-19).
- Aisha (QA) — run the staging rehearsal script and validate both event counts and UI states (2027-05-19 am).

Canary rehearsal checklist (short):
- Pre-checks (30m before): canary infra up, DB migrations none, rollback route available.
- Telemetry smoke (5m): fire 100 synthetic panel-applies, verify ingestion counts within expected tolerance.
- UI verification (10m): verify spinner -> help tooltip text, confirm rollout id visible.
- Observability (10m): validate kv-warmup events, ensure no duplicate alerts during partial applies.
- Rollback test (5m): trigger rollback path and ensure metrics revert and alert noise suppressed.

Risks / open questions:
- Will aligning sampling affect historical dashboards? Short-term yes; need to document the adjustment and annotate dashboards so analysts know counts changed. Owner: Marco.
- Performance: adding kv-warmup telemetry adds small payloads; estimate +0.2% CPU on frontend at peak — check with infra. Owner: Ethan to confirm.
- Operator experience: do we prefer an explicit progress bar vs better microcopy? Design trade-off — Leah to prototype quick bar if microcopy doesn't reduce incidents after the canary.

Notes to self / loose thoughts (brain dump):
- Consider a small helper view that maps rollout id -> last 5 backend log lines in the panel UI (would make ops reconciliation fast). Probably a small backend endpoint plus short TTL cache. Tracked as follow-up if this pattern repeats.
- Might be worth a small analytics job to backfill correct counts for the affected window (2027-05-12 -> 2027-05-18). If we don't backfill, multi-day reports will be inaccurate. Add to analytics backlog.

Follow-ups / next sync:
- Canary rehearsal 2027-05-19 09:30 PT (owners to be present). Quick sync 30m after rehearsal to decide rollout.
- Postmortem-style note if mismatch persists; keep doc open for updates.

Linked references (in-chat):
- Linear: RO-3421 (gate telemetry mismatch)
- GitHub: PR #1876 (UI microcopy)
- Slack: convo in #console-ops (thread started 2027-05-17)

Raw checklist for staging run (QA):
- [ ] Deploy telemetry override to staging
- [ ] Deploy UI microcopy PR to staging
- [ ] Deploy kv-warmup telemetry feature flag
- [ ] Run synthetic 100 events and compare counts
- [ ] Validate UI shows rollout id and updated tooltip
- [ ] Confirm no duplicate alerts fired

End notes: keep this doc as the single source of truth for the rehearsal day. I'll update with timestamps and quick outcomes after the 09:30 run.

-- Samira
